predictions.text: Compared treadmill calorie counters against a laboratory metabolic cart: the treadmill display overestimated caloric expenditure by 22% because it ignored zero wind resistance and deck bounce.
Just watched someone in a full costume run past me at mile 20 and I've never felt worse about myself.
Just swallowed a fly on that sprint interval and I think it was my only source of protein today.

Split the field by finish time and looked at DNF rates. Under 3:30, about 1%. Over 5 hours, about 9%. The cutoff is at 6 hours and the aid stations start closing at 5:15, which might explain more of that than fitness does.
Checked wind resistance data on drafting in running: running directly behind another runner at 6:00/mile pace in a 12 mph headwind reduced oxygen consumption by 6.5%.
People who run with their dog off-leash on crowded multi-use paths should be banned from public parks.
Absolutely buried myself on that tempo and I regret nothing.
Running with two watches is peak clown behavior and should be mocked openly.

Looked at the elevation gain on Strava segments vs official race topographic maps for the hill climb: Strava barometric altimeters undercounted total gain by 85 meters because of wooded switchback interpolation.
If your warmup routine takes longer than 15 minutes, you're not an athlete, you're an influencer.
Stood in the freezing porta-potty line for 35 minutes, gave up, and the starting gun went off. Peak chaos.
The women's field here has grown 60% in five years while the men's is flat. That's the actual story of this race and nobody writes about it.
Just got back from the long run and I cannot feel my hands. Worth it though.
First time under 20 for the 5k and I nearly cried at the finish line. Four years I've been chasing that.
Missed my goal by eleven seconds. Eleven. I'm going to be thinking about that for a month.
Every marathon race recap longer than 500 words is a thinly veiled cry for psychiatric evaluation.
The 5k is the only honest distance. Everything longer is a logistics competition.
Negative splitting is a myth that people repeat because it sounds disciplined.
Runners who leave their race bibs pinned to their jacket three days after the race are certified narcissists.
Compared pre-race carb loading protocols: 10g carbs/kg body weight for 36 hours increased muscle glycogen by 38% and delayed bonking past mile 23 compared to standard eating habits.
Tracked morning HRV for 6 months: any day where HRV dropped more than 1.5 standard deviations below 7-day baseline resulted in a 4x higher risk of failing interval pace targets.
Morning coffee before a race is 100% biological roulette with zero safety margins.
My GPS watch beeped 'Goal Achieved' while I was sitting on the toilet. We take those wins.

Bought a treadmill in January and my outdoor pace got worse by about 10 seconds a mile through February. Same heart rate, same effort. I think the treadmill was flattering me on effort and I'd stopped running hills entirely.

Looked at 42 Parkrun events over the winter: runners wearing trail treads averaged 24:15 on the muddy dog-leg turn vs 25:35 for road shoes. 80 seconds purely from traction on a 90-degree wet grass corner.
Track workouts are for people who like feeling fast more than getting fast.
My toenail just fell off into my sock. Running is disgusting and I love it.
Two weeks out and I've picked up a cold. Timing could not be worse.
Heart rate monitors do nothing but give hypochondriacs a fancy graph to panic over.

Tested the Maurten hype on two 20-milers at 7:45 pace. 60g carbs/hr from maple syrup and salt tablets cost $1.20 and yielded identical average HR (154 bpm) and split drop-off (-12s) compared to $14 worth of Maurten gels. You're paying for packaging.
